newsitem.title: USA: Montana row crop harvest nearly finished.
newsitem.headline: Montana row crop harvest nearly finished.

text.p: Row crop harvest was virtually completed and many areas of Montana received much needed moisture during the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop report.

Winter wheat was 99 percent planted against 95 percent a week earlier, last year's 97 percent and the average of 93 percent. Wheat had emerged on 70 percent of the acreage, up from 61 a week earlier and ahead of the 70 percent average.
Soil moisture conditions improved from a week ago, the report said. Topsoil moisture was rated four percent very short, 42 percent short, 45 percent adequate and 9 percent surplus.
The sugar beet crop was 97 percent harvested, against 91 percent a week earlier, 95 percent last year and the 88 percent average.

Pasture and range was rated 5 percent very poor, 29 percent poor, 36 percent fair, 29 percent good and one percent excellent. By the weekend, 76 percent of the cattle and calves were moved off summer ranges.
